issue.title: Rich-text editor splits URLs at the question mark, creating nonfunctional hyperlinks
issue.body:
### Information about bug

I am experiencing an issue in ERPNext/Frappe v15 where URLs containing query parameters are incorrectly converted into divided hyperlinks by rich-text editor fields.

**Environment**
Frappe Framework: v15.101.5
ERPNext: v15.100.1
Browser: Google Chrome 150.0.7871.187, 64-bit
Operating system: Windows 10

**Example URL**

The issue can be reproduced using this nonfunctional example URL:

https://example.com?invid=TEST123456

**Actual behavior**

When the URL is pasted into a rich-text editor field, only the portion before the question mark becomes part of the hyperlink:

https://example.com

The following portion is displayed as plain text immediately after the hyperlink:

?invid=TEST123456

The result appears visually as one continuous URL, but the actual hyperlink points only to:

https://example.com

The query parameter is excluded from the hyperlink.

**Steps to reproduce**

Open any ERPNext or Frappe field that uses the rich-text editor.
Paste the following URL:
https://example.com?invid=TEST123456

Observe that only https://example.com becomes a hyperlink.
The text ?invid=TEST123456 remains outside the hyperlink.

The same behavior occurs when using Paste as plain text:

Paste the URL as plain text into the rich-text editor.
Initially, the entire URL remains plain text.
Press the Return or Enter key.
The editor automatically converts the URL into a hyperlink.
The hyperlink is again divided at the question mark.

**Email Template behavior**

The problem is not limited to URLs manually pasted into an outgoing email.

When an Email Template inserts a URL containing a query parameter, the generated email also contains the divided hyperlink.

If the email is sent from ERPNext, the divided hyperlink remains incorrect and nonfunctional for the recipient. Only the portion before the question mark is clickable.

**Expected behavior**

The rich-text editor should recognize the entire URL, including its query string, as one hyperlink:

https://example.com?invid=TEST123456

The hyperlink destination should include:

?invid=TEST123456

**Additional information**

The same URL is converted correctly when pasted into Microsoft Word or Gmail.

This issue affects payment links and potentially any URL that depends on query parameters. In our case, the omitted query parameter identifies the specific payment request, so excluding it makes the resulting hyperlink unusable.

Has anyone else encountered this behavior in Frappe or ERPNext v15? Is this a known rich-text editor issue, or is there a configuration or sanitization setting that controls URL detection?

### Module

other

### Version

Frappe Framework: v15.101.5
ERPNext: v15.100.1
Browser: Google Chrome 150.0.7871.187, 64-bit
Operating system: Windows 10

issue.title: fix(attach): Skip auto-save when attaching files on unsaved documents
issue.body:
Guard `frm.save()` calls in `on_upload_complete` and `clear_attachment` with `!frm.is_new()` so that uploading or clearing an attachment on a new (unsaved) document does not trigger the full save pipeline and mandatory field validation.

Fixes #39480

Credits to: @musabaku

comment.body: @greptile-apps the persisted file becoming orphaned is a pre-existing issue and saving it during attach is not the right way to handle orphaned file issue. It will create more side-effects than solving this issue

Doing save once user uploads can cause validation error if the mandatory fields are empty.  This guard causes more issue and makes user abandon from creating new entry. Relinking the persisted file will happen during actual save flow.

issue.title: Chart legend overlaps when legend labels are long
issue.body: ## Description of the issue The chart legend overlaps when legend labels are long. Instead of maintaining proper spacing or wrapping to the next line, legend items are rendered on top of each other, making the legend difficult to read. This issue is reproducible with the built-in Pie Chart (and likely other chart types using the same legend component) when multiple legend items have relatively long labels. ## Context information (for bug reports) **Output of `bench version`** ``` frappe 16.22.0 ``` ## Steps to reproduce the issue 1. Create a Pie Chart using the Frappe Charts component. 2. Add multiple legend items with long labels, for example: - Deluxe Double Room - Deluxe Triple Room - Reservation - Spa 3. Render the chart in a dashboard or page. For further clarification, See the image below, ### Observed result - Legend items overlap each other horizontally. - Long labels are rendered on top of adjacent legend items. - The legend becomes unreadable, especially on narrower containers. ### Expected result - Legend items should maintain proper spacing. - If there isn't enough horizontal space, legend items should automatically wrap onto the next line. - The legend should remain readable and responsive regardless of the label length or container width. ### Stacktrace / full error message ``` No error is thrown. This is a UI rendering/layout issue. ``` ## Additional information - OS: macOS - Browser: Google Chrome (latest)

issue.title: Convert frappe.session from untyped _dict to typed Session/SessionData classes
issue.body:
## Problem
frappe.session was typed as _dict[str, Any], providing no type safety for the many attributes accessed throughout the codebase (user, sid, data.user_type, data.csrf_token, etc.).
## Solution
Introduced two new types in frappe/types/session.py:
- SessionData — a @dataclass for frappe.session.data with typed fields (user, session_ip, user_agent, user_type, csrf_token, impersonated_by, etc.) and dict-compatible methods (__getitem__, get, update) for backward compatibility.
- Session — extends _dict[str, Any] with typed annotations for the top-level attributes (user: str, sid: str, data: SessionData), maintaining full dict compatibility for existing access patterns like session["user"] and session.get(...).
## Backward Compatibility
- Session extends _dict, so all existing dict-like access (session["user"], session.get(...), session.update(...)) continues to work.
- SessionData provides __getitem__, get, update, keys, values, items for code that accesses session.data with dict patterns.

issue.title: `UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed` in `sqlite_search._index_documents` aborts document save
issue.body:
# `UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed` in `sqlite_search._index_documents` aborts document save (and, via on-save indexing, the whole caller)

## Summary

`SQLiteSearch._index_documents()` passes text field values straight into
`cursor.executemany()`. If any indexed text field contains a Unicode **surrogate
code point** (U+D800–U+DFFF), the `sqlite3` driver fails to encode the bound
parameter as UTF-8 and raises:

```
UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 0-1: surrogates not allowed
```

Because indexing runs from the `on_update` document hook
(`frappe.search.sqlite_search.update_doc_index`), the exception propagates out of
`Document.save()` and aborts the **entire operation that triggered the save**, not
just the index write.

## Impact

This is not limited to a degraded search index. When the save happens inside a
background pipeline, the whole unit of work is rolled back and retried, turning a
single bad record into a poison pill.

Concrete real-world case: an inbound e-mail whose HTML body starts with an emoji
that arrived as mis-encoded UTF-16 surrogate code points (common with Outlook /
Exchange). The Helpdesk app indexes `Communication`, so on
`pull_from_email_account → mail.process() → communication.save() → on_update →
update_doc_index → index_doc → _index_documents → cursor.executemany()` the save
raises, `EmailAccount.receive()` re-raises, and the pull job rolls back. The mail
is never persisted and is re-fetched on every poll cycle, so a legitimate customer
e-mail is silently blocked and the error recurs indefinitely.

## Environment

- Frappe: reproduced against `version-15` (raise at
  `frappe/search/sqlite_search.py`, `_index_documents`, `cursor.executemany`).
  Same code path is present on `develop`.
- Trigger app: Frappe Helpdesk (registers a `SQLiteSearch` subclass over
  `Communication` via the `sqlite_search` hook), but the defect is in the
  framework indexer and affects any `SQLiteSearch` subclass.

## Traceback (payload redacted)

```
File "frappe/email/doctype/email_account/email_account.py", in receive
  communication = mail.process()
File "frappe/email/receive.py", in _build_communication_doc
  communication.save()
File "frappe/model/document.py", in run_post_save_methods
  self.run_method("on_update")
File "frappe/search/sqlite_search.py", in update_doc_index
  search.index_doc(doctype, doc.name)
File "frappe/search/sqlite_search.py", in _index_documents
  cursor.executemany(insert_sql, values_to_insert)
UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 0-1: surrogates not allowed
```

## Minimal reproduction

The root cause is that SQLite (like UTF-8 in general) rejects surrogate code
points in bound string parameters:

```python
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
con.execute("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING fts5(content)")

# "\ud83d\udc4d" is a valid UTF-16 surrogate pair for U+1F44D (thumbs up) that
# ended up as two surrogate code points inside a Python str (e.g. after a
# mis-decode of an inbound e-mail body).
con.executemany("INSERT INTO t (content) VALUES (?)", [("\ud83d\udc4d hello",)])
# -> UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 0-1:
#    surrogates not allowed
```

In Frappe this is hit whenever such a value reaches
`SQLiteSearch._index_documents()` (real-time via `update_doc_index`, or during a
full `build_index`), and also `_build_vocabulary_incremental()` which does
`executemany(...)` into `search_trigrams` with words derived from the same text.

## Root cause

The indexer never sanitises text before handing it to SQLite. Any surrogate code
point in `content` / `title` / a custom text field (or, defensively, any metadata
column) makes `executemany()` raise.

## Suggested fix

Add a small helper that repairs or drops surrogate code points and apply it at
the two text sinks. A round-trip through UTF-16 with `surrogatepass` re-pairs
valid surrogate **pairs** back into their real astral character (so a
mis-encoded emoji is preserved rather than lost), and a following UTF-8 `ignore`
pass removes any remaining **lone** surrogate. A cheap regex fast-path keeps the
common (surrogate-free) case allocation-free.

A `git am`-applicable patch is attached (`surrogate_fix.patch`, against
`develop`). The three hunks:

```diff
+SURROGATE_RE = re.compile(r"[\ud800-\udfff]")
+
+
+def strip_surrogates(value):
+	"""Repair or drop Unicode surrogate code points so a value can be encoded as UTF-8.
+	... (docstring) ...
+	"""
+	if not isinstance(value, str) or not SURROGATE_RE.search(value):
+		return value
+	return (
+		value.encode("utf-16-le", "surrogatepass")
+		.decode("utf-16-le", "surrogatepass")
+		.encode("utf-8", "ignore")
+		.decode("utf-8")
+	)
```

```diff
 						else:
-							values.append(doc.get(field, ""))
+							values.append(strip_surrogates(doc.get(field, "")))
```

```diff
 		text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()  # normalize whitespace
+		text = strip_surrogates(text)  # drop/repair UTF-16 surrogate code points
 		return text
```

The `_process_content` hunk covers the FTS `content`/`title` columns and the
trigram vocabulary path; the `_index_documents` hunk is a defensive guard right
at the DB boundary so no metadata column can reach `executemany()` with a
surrogate either. Maintainers who prefer a single change can keep just the
`_process_content` hunk, which fixes the reported crash.

Behaviour of `strip_surrogates` (verified):

| input | output | note |
|---|---|---|
| `"\ud83d\udc4d Th"` (surrogate pair) | `"\U0001F44D Th"` | emoji recovered |
| `"x\ud83dy"` (lone high) | `"xy"` | lone surrogate dropped |
| `"a\udc4db"` (lone low) | `"ab"` | lone surrogate dropped |
| `"\U0001F600 c"` (valid astral) | unchanged | no-op |
| `"Hallo"` | unchanged | fast-path, no round-trip |
| non-`str` (int/None) | unchanged | returned as-is |

issue.title: `UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed` in `sqlite_search._index_documents` aborts document save
issue.body:
# `UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed` in `sqlite_search._index_documents` aborts document save (and, via on-save indexing, the whole caller)

## Summary

`SQLiteSearch._index_documents()` passes text field values straight into
`cursor.executemany()`. If any indexed text field contains a Unicode **surrogate
code point** (U+D800–U+DFFF), the `sqlite3` driver fails to encode the bound
parameter as UTF-8 and raises:

```
UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 0-1: surrogates not allowed
```

Because indexing runs from the `on_update` document hook
(`frappe.search.sqlite_search.update_doc_index`), the exception propagates out of
`Document.save()` and aborts the **entire operation that triggered the save**, not
just the index write.

## Impact

This is not limited to a degraded search index. When the save happens inside a
background pipeline, the whole unit of work is rolled back and retried, turning a
single bad record into a poison pill.

Concrete real-world case: an inbound e-mail whose HTML body starts with an emoji
that arrived as mis-encoded UTF-16 surrogate code points (common with Outlook /
Exchange). The Helpdesk app indexes `Communication`, so on
`pull_from_email_account → mail.process() → communication.save() → on_update →
update_doc_index → index_doc → _index_documents → cursor.executemany()` the save
raises, `EmailAccount.receive()` re-raises, and the pull job rolls back. The mail
is never persisted and is re-fetched on every poll cycle, so a legitimate customer
e-mail is silently blocked and the error recurs indefinitely.

## Environment

- Frappe: reproduced against `version-15` (raise at
  `frappe/search/sqlite_search.py`, `_index_documents`, `cursor.executemany`).
  Same code path is present on `develop`.
- Trigger app: Frappe Helpdesk (registers a `SQLiteSearch` subclass over
  `Communication` via the `sqlite_search` hook), but the defect is in the
  framework indexer and affects any `SQLiteSearch` subclass.

## Traceback (payload redacted)

```
File "frappe/email/doctype/email_account/email_account.py", in receive
  communication = mail.process()
File "frappe/email/receive.py", in _build_communication_doc
  communication.save()
File "frappe/model/document.py", in run_post_save_methods
  self.run_method("on_update")
File "frappe/search/sqlite_search.py", in update_doc_index
  search.index_doc(doctype, doc.name)
File "frappe/search/sqlite_search.py", in _index_documents
  cursor.executemany(insert_sql, values_to_insert)
UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 0-1: surrogates not allowed
```

## Minimal reproduction

The root cause is that SQLite (like UTF-8 in general) rejects surrogate code
points in bound string parameters:

```python
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
con.execute("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING fts5(content)")

# "\ud83d\udc4d" is a valid UTF-16 surrogate pair for U+1F44D (thumbs up) that
# ended up as two surrogate code points inside a Python str (e.g. after a
# mis-decode of an inbound e-mail body).
con.executemany("INSERT INTO t (content) VALUES (?)", [("\ud83d\udc4d hello",)])
# -> UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 0-1:
#    surrogates not allowed
```

In Frappe this is hit whenever such a value reaches
`SQLiteSearch._index_documents()` (real-time via `update_doc_index`, or during a
full `build_index`), and also `_build_vocabulary_incremental()` which does
`executemany(...)` into `search_trigrams` with words derived from the same text.

## Root cause

The indexer never sanitises text before handing it to SQLite. Any surrogate code
point in `content` / `title` / a custom text field (or, defensively, any metadata
column) makes `executemany()` raise.

## Suggested fix

Add a small helper that repairs or drops surrogate code points and apply it at
the two text sinks. A round-trip through UTF-16 with `surrogatepass` re-pairs
valid surrogate **pairs** back into their real astral character (so a
mis-encoded emoji is preserved rather than lost), and a following UTF-8 `ignore`
pass removes any remaining **lone** surrogate. A cheap regex fast-path keeps the
common (surrogate-free) case allocation-free.

A `git am`-applicable patch is attached (`surrogate_fix.patch`, against
`develop`). The three hunks:

```diff
+SURROGATE_RE = re.compile(r"[\ud800-\udfff]")
+
+
+def strip_surrogates(value):
+	"""Repair or drop Unicode surrogate code points so a value can be encoded as UTF-8.
+	... (docstring) ...
+	"""
+	if not isinstance(value, str) or not SURROGATE_RE.search(value):
+		return value
+	return (
+		value.encode("utf-16-le", "surrogatepass")
+		.decode("utf-16-le", "surrogatepass")
+		.encode("utf-8", "ignore")
+		.decode("utf-8")
+	)
```

```diff
 						else:
-							values.append(doc.get(field, ""))
+							values.append(strip_surrogates(doc.get(field, "")))
```

```diff
 		text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()  # normalize whitespace
+		text = strip_surrogates(text)  # drop/repair UTF-16 surrogate code points
 		return text
```

The `_process_content` hunk covers the FTS `content`/`title` columns and the
trigram vocabulary path; the `_index_documents` hunk is a defensive guard right
at the DB boundary so no metadata column can reach `executemany()` with a
surrogate either. Maintainers who prefer a single change can keep just the
`_process_content` hunk, which fixes the reported crash.

Behaviour of `strip_surrogates` (verified):

| input | output | note |
|---|---|---|
| `"\ud83d\udc4d Th"` (surrogate pair) | `"\U0001F44D Th"` | emoji recovered |
| `"x\ud83dy"` (lone high) | `"xy"` | lone surrogate dropped |
| `"a\udc4db"` (lone low) | `"ab"` | lone surrogate dropped |
| `"\U0001F600 c"` (valid astral) | unchanged | no-op |
| `"Hallo"` | unchanged | fast-path, no round-trip |
| non-`str` (int/None) | unchanged | returned as-is |

Happy to open a PR with this change if useful.
[surrogate_fix.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30232469/surrogate_fix.patch)

issue.title: feat: Add Interactive Hover Tooltips for Form Fields (End-User & Developer Modes)
issue.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, Frappe forms lack interactive field-level tooltips when users hover over fields. Users have to rely entirely on documentation or small sub-text labels which can clutter the user interface.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to propose two types of hover tooltips for form fields:
1. **For End-Users (Implementation Mode):** Instead of displaying long description text below the field, we can add a small info icon (i) next to the label. Hovering over it should trigger a Bootstrap tooltip/popover showing the field description.
2. **For Developers/Consultants (Learning Mode):** When navigating the system in Developer Mode, hovering over a field should show a tooltip with its technical details (e.g., `Fieldname`, `Fieldtype`). This will help people transitioning from other ERPs to explore Frappe easily without constantly shifting to documentation.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using standard field descriptions below each input, but it clutter the forms and doesn't provide a clean enterprise-grade UX.

**Additional context**
A global system setting or localStorage toggle like "Enable Field Tooltips" can be added so users can turn it off if they prefer a cleaner UI.

issue.title: Workspace header blocks (Reports & Masters) not translatable — hardcoded HTML in content JSON

labels.name: invalid
labels.description: Question about using Frappe apps or bench

issue.body: ## Description Workspace pages contain header blocks with hardcoded HTML text in the `content` JSON field. These strings are not passed through `_()` and cannot be translated via PO files or Translation DocType. The most common example is the **"Reports & Masters"** header that appears on nearly every module page (Buying, Selling, Stock, Manufacturing, Projects, etc.). ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Set system language to any non-English language (e.g., Polish) 2. Navigate to any module page, e.g., `/app/buying` 3. Observe the "Reports & Masters" section header — it remains in English ## Expected Behavior Section headers on Workspace pages should be translatable. ## Actual Behavior The header text is stored as raw HTML inside the Workspace `content` JSON field: ```json { "type": "header", "data": { "text": "Reports & Masters", "col": 12 } } ``` Since this is a hardcoded HTML string in a JSON blob, it never passes through `_()` or `__()`. The PO translation exists (`"Reports & Masters"` → `"Raporty i dane podstawowe"` in Polish), but is never applied. ## Affected Workspaces All module Workspaces with header blocks: Assets, Buying, Home, Invoicing, Manufacturing, Projects, Quality, Selling, Support (9 total in a default ERPNext installation). ## Suggested Fix When rendering Workspace header blocks on the frontend, pass the text content through `__()` before inserting into the DOM. The PO translation already exists — it just needs to be applied. Alternatively, store header text as a translatable key rather than raw HTML. ## Workaround Direct SQL update of the `content` field in `tabWorkspace`: ```python frappe.db.sql("UPDATE `tabWorkspace` SET content = REPLACE(content, 'Reports & Masters', 'Raporty i dane podstawowe') WHERE content LIKE '%Reports & Masters%'") ``` ## Version - Frappe: v16.24.3 - ERPNext: v16.25.0

   maintainers to reproduce, the faster it'll be fixed.
4. If you think you know what the reason for the bug is, share it with us. Maybe put in a PR 😉
-->

## Description of the issue
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith' in create_desktop_icons_from_workspace() when an App-type Desktop Icon has no link

```python
if icon.label == app_title and (
    app_icon and frappe.db.get_value("Desktop Icon", app_icon, "link").startswith("/app")
):
``` 
`frappe.db.get_value("Desktop Icon", app_icon, "link") ` can return None when the App-type Desktop Icon record has no link value set. The code calls .startswith("/app") on that result directly, with no None-check, causing an AttributeError.

Contrast with the near-identical check a few lines above (258-260):

```python
if frappe.db.get_value("Desktop Icon", app_icon, "link") and not frappe.db.get_value(
    "Desktop Icon", app_icon, "link"
).startswith("/app"):
``` 
which happens to be safe only because of the leading truthy check short-circuiting — but it calls `get_value` twice redundantly, which is itself worth cleaning up in the same fix.


##Suggested fix: 
cache `frappe.db.get_value("Desktop Icon", app_icon, "link")` once in a local variable and guard both checks (258-260 and 266) against `None `before calling` .startswith().`

`frappe/desk/doctype/desktop_icon/desktop_icon.py`, lines 264-269 (inside `create_desktop_icons_from_workspace()`)

issue.title: Frappe UI bug
issue.body: Duration picker is incorrectly positioned inside editable child tables When using a Duration field inside an editable child table (Grid), the Time Spent picker (Days / Hours / Minutes / Seconds) appears in the wrong location on the page. Instead of opening next to the focused input, the popup is rendered elsewhere in the form, making it difficult to use. This is a Frappe UI bug, not a DocType configuration issue. Steps to Reproduce Create a DocType with a child table. Add a Duration field to the child DocType. Enable Editable Grid. scrool down to the form Focus the Duration field. Click the picker icon. Expected Behavior The Time Spent picker should appear adjacent to the focused Duration input within the grid. Actual Behavior The picker is displayed at an incorrect position, often detached from the active cell. Root Cause ControlDuration renders the Time Spent picker with position: fixed, but its top and left coordinates are not calculated when the control is used inside an editable grid. As a result, the browser positions the popup incorrectly. Proposed Fix Update ControlDuration to position the picker relative to the focused input using getBoundingClientRect(). For example: Get the active input element. Read its bounding rectangle using getBoundingClientRect(). Set the popup's top and left values accordingly. Recalculate the position on scroll or resize if necessary. This keeps the picker correctly aligned regardless of whether the Duration field is used in a standard form or inside an editable child table. Environment Frappe Framework: v16 (also worth verifying on other supported versions) Browser: Any (reproducible in Chromium-based browsers)

For example: Get the active input element. Read its bounding rectangle using getBoundingClientRect(). Set the popup's top and left values accordingly. Recalculate the position on scroll or resize if necessary. This keeps the picker correctly aligned regardless of whether the Duration field is used in a standard form or inside an editable child table. Environment Frappe Framework: v16 (also worth verifying on other supported versions) Browser: Any (reproducible in Chromium-based browsers)
